node.title: Re: perl 5.32 format question
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I reduced your code down to this test case: perl -e '$_=" "; formline q{^<<<~~}, $_; length $^A or die' and a [id://11110663|bisect] reported that "[https://github.com/Perl/perl5/commit/9b4bdfd44e0e6d44a447f231c281f967c7ca35c9|9b4bdfd4] is the first bad commit". This is a commit that fixes several bugs in formats; it was first released as part of Perl v5.20.0 9 years ago.

If you read the documentation, note that a [doc://perlform#Repeating-Format-Lines|double tilde] means "the line will be repeated until all the fields on the line are exhausted, i.e. undefined", however, a [doc://perlform#Suppressing-Lines-Where-All-Fields-Are-Void|single tilde] "anywhere in the line" means to suppress "lines where all fields are blank". Although I think the documentation could be a lot more clear on this (Update: [https://github.com/Perl/perl5/pull/21130|patch applied]), a double tilde implies the single tilde, as is confirmed by [https://github.com/Perl/perl5/blob/perl-5.000/pp_ctl.c#L2207|the relevant code in Perl 5.0.0] and [https://github.com/Perl/perl5/blob/v5.36.1/pp_ctl.c#L5638|today].

Anyway, the following provides your expected output both on older and recent Perl versions (tested on 5.14 to 5.36):

format REP = ^<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< $rep_line ^<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< ~~ $rep_line .
